ios.head: No big App Total Revenue swing expected in about 7 days — the share of installs that become subs is normal.
ios.body: App Total New Subs is -10.0% and App Total Install is -4.5%; the gap between them (-5.5pp) is under the 10pp we treat as a real signal, so the share of people who install and then subscribe is close to normal. New subs start as 7-day free trials, so today's new subs are next period's App Total Revenue. So nothing unusual is building up that would swing App Total Revenue in about 7 days.

insights.title: Revenue by purchase type — App Total Revenue -6.4% — down mainly in Subscription (-4,825, -5.6%).
insights.body: App Total Revenue was 84,959, against 90,743 for the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks (-5,783). By purchase type: Subscription -4,825 (-5.6%), Pay as you go -958 (-19.4%). Pay as you go is 4.7% of revenue. Subscription is the recurring part fed by new subs about a week earlier; look at new subs and renewals.

insights.title: Purchase type by app — Subscription revenue is falling most in YMK (-5.9%).
insights.body: By app: the biggest Subscription fall is YMK -2,331 (-5.9%, about 44% of revenue); Pay as you go moved most in YCP -395 (-23.6%); YCV relies most on Pay as you go (14% of its revenue vs 4.7% overall). Subscription is the recurring revenue that new subs feed; Pay as you go is one-off spend.

insights.title: Installs to subs, by app — YMK is turning installs into New Subs worse than usual (-12.8% vs Install -2.0%).
insights.body: Some apps are not converting installs into subscribers at their usual rate: YMK New Subs -12.8% vs Install -2.0% (worse than its installs). Revenue follows about a week later, so these are the apps to watch next week.

insights.title: Which app — App Total Revenue is down in every app — something is affecting all of them, not one.
insights.body: App Total Revenue is down in every app (All App -6.4%, YMK -6.1%, YCP -5.2%, YCV -6.2%). When all apps move together the cause is usually something they share — the season, an app-store change, or how the data is collected — rather than any one app's own doing.

insights.title: Install source — App Total Install -3.6% — Paid Install is behind most of it (-617, -4.9%).
insights.body: App Total Install was 27,557, against 28,590 for the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks — a change of -1,033. Where that came from: Paid Install -617 (-4.9%), SEO Install -533 (-24.8%), Organic Install +138 (+1.0%). Paid Install moved the most on its own (-617, -4.9%) and is now 43.2% of all installs, so that is the channel to look at first.

insights.title: Install mix — Where installs come from is shifting away from SEO Install (-24.8% vs -3.6% for installs overall).
insights.body: SEO Install was 1,615, -24.8% against the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks, while total installs moved -3.6% — a difference of -21.2 percentage points. SEO Install is now 5.9% of all installs, so the balance between channels is moving away from it; free traffic slipping while paid holds up means we are buying more of the same installs..

insights.title: Purchase type by country — Subscription revenue is falling most in JP (-27.3%), while US grows (+5.0%).
insights.body: By country: the biggest Subscription fall is JP -1,125 (-27.3%, about 4% of revenue); the biggest Subscription gain is US +1,676 (+5.0%); Pay as you go moved most in JP -504 (-40.2%); JP relies most on Pay as you go (20% of its revenue vs 4.7% overall). Subscription is the recurring revenue that new subs feed; Pay as you go is one-off spend.

insights.title: Revenue vs new subs — App Total Revenue +7.5% — up in line with the new subs signed up 7 days earlier (+1.9%).
insights.body: App Total Revenue on 10-16 vs 10-09 is +7.5%, and App Total New Subs on 10-09 vs 10-02 was +1.9% — both moved the same way. Most new subs start as a 7-day free trial, so the subscription revenue landing now mostly comes from people who subscribed about 7 days ago. By purchase type (on 10-16 vs 10-09): Subscription +9.6%, Pay as you go -22.6%. This is the normal pattern, so no surprise is building up.

insights.title: Which country — US is out of line with every other country on App Total Revenue (+4.9% vs -6.4%).
insights.body: For All App, App Total Revenue in US is +4.9% while all countries together are -6.4% — a gap of +11.2pp. US is about 43% of revenue, so it is big enough to be worth a look.
